measures.label: Population
measures.what: How many people live in each suburb, as each census counted them. Between censuses the map reads a straight line from one count to the next.
measures.note: The people who usually live in the suburb, within its boundaries in each census year.

source.label: ABS Census 2011, 2016 and 2021, DataPacks by suburb (CC BY 4.0)

measures.label: People per square kilometre
measures.what: How closely people live: each census's count over the suburb's whole area.
measures.note: The area takes in parks, golf courses, rail yards and university grounds, so a suburb with much open space reads sparser than its streets are.

source.label: ABS Census 2011, 2016 and 2021, DataPacks by suburb (CC BY 4.0)

measures.label: Median household income
measures.what: The weekly income of the household in the middle: half the suburb's households take home more, half less. In the dollars of each census year, not adjusted for inflation.
measures.note: Households that did not state their income are left out of the median.

source.label: ABS Census 2011, 2016 and 2021, DataPacks by suburb (CC BY 4.0)

measures.label: Residents with a university degree
measures.what: The share of residents aged 15 and over whose highest qualification is a bachelor's degree or higher: graduate diplomas and certificates, master's degrees and doctorates.
measures.note: It counts students still at school or university too, so a suburb with many young residents reads lower than its adults' schooling.

source.label: ABS Census 2011, 2016 and 2021, DataPacks by suburb (CC BY 4.0)

measures.label: Recorded crime
measures.what: Offences against people and property that police recorded in the suburb in a year, for every 1,000 people who live there: assault, sexual offences, robbery, break and enter, theft, malicious damage and the like.
measures.note: Counted against residents, so places many more people visit than live in (the city centre, Haymarket, Bondi Beach, Manly) read high. Offences police find by looking, such as drug possession, are left out, and so is fraud. Suburbs of fewer than 300 residents have no rate.

source.label: NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, criminal incidents by suburb (CC BY 4.0)

measures.label: Median house price
measures.what: The price in the middle of a year's sales of houses and other homes on their own land, in the dollars of the year.
measures.note: By postcode, so suburbs that share a postcode share a price (Sydney, Haymarket, The Rocks, Millers Point and Barangaroo are all 2000). A quarter of 10 or fewer sales has no median and is left out, and so is a year of fewer than 20.

source.label: NSW Department of Communities and Justice, Rent and Sales Report, by postcode (CC BY 4.0)

measures.label: Median apartment price
measures.what: The price in the middle of a year's sales of apartments, townhouses and other strata homes, in the dollars of the year.
measures.note: By postcode, so suburbs that share a postcode share a price (Sydney, Haymarket, The Rocks, Millers Point and Barangaroo are all 2000). A quarter of 10 or fewer sales has no median and is left out, and so is a year of fewer than 20.

source.label: NSW Department of Communities and Justice, Rent and Sales Report, by postcode (CC BY 4.0)
